page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0, both falling into the bottom 25% or lower. However, multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 11776.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5757.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.85 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. The instance handles database operations and static web serving adequately, achieving 11.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 7.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is its modest single-threaded compute capability, which limits its suitability for single-core bottlenecked tasks. However, its high memory density makes it a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for workloads such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, multi-threaded data processing, and moderate web serving.
